# Gatherly — project rules

Gatherly is an event and ticketing app (organizers publish events, attendees
reserve tickets and check in with a QR code). It is built step by step by a
student during a 10-class **Next.js 16 App Router** course. The person you are
helping is **learning** this stack.

## Your training data is out of date for this project

This stack is newer than most of what you were trained on. Next.js 14/15,
Tailwind 3, Zod 3, Drizzle 1.0 RC docs and NextAuth tutorials are all **wrong
here**. When unsure about a Next.js API, read the docs bundled with the
installed version in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`, or the package's own type
definitions — not your memory.

## Pinned stack — do not upgrade

| Package                       | Version                              | Notes                                                             |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `next`                        | 16.3.x                               | App Router only. Turbopack for `dev` and `build`                  |
| `react` / `react-dom`         | 19.3.x                               |                                                                   |
| `typescript`                  | **6.0.x — not 7**                    | `typescript-eslint` does not support TS 7; `npm run lint` crashes |
| `eslint`                      | **9.x — not 10**                     | `eslint-plugin-react` crashes on ESLint 10                        |
| `tailwindcss`                 | 4.x                                  | CSS-first. There is no `tailwind.config.*`                        |
| `drizzle-orm` / `drizzle-kit` | **0.45.x** / 0.31.x — **not 1.0 RC** | With `pg` (node-postgres), not `postgres.js`                      |
| `better-auth`                 | 1.7.x                                | Not NextAuth / Auth.js                                            |
| `zod`                         | 4.x                                  | Not the v3 API                                                    |
| `shadcn` (CLI)                | latest                               | The package is `shadcn`, never `shadcn-ui`                        |

- Only use packages already listed in `package.json`. If a task needs a new dependency, **ask first** and say why.
- A rule below may describe a library the project has not installed yet (the database arrives in class 03, auth in class 06). Do not install it early — ask.
- Never "upgrade everything to latest". Check `npm view <pkg> peerDependencies` first.

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev        # dev server on http://localhost:3000
npm run build      # production build; prints the route table (○ static, ƒ dynamic)
npm run check      # typecheck + lint + format check — must pass
npm run lint:fix   # auto-fix lint errors
npm run format     # format every file with Prettier
```

Database scripts (`db:generate`, `db:migrate`, `db:seed`, `db:studio`) exist from class 03.

**Every change must pass `npm run check`.** Run it before you say a task is done,
and fix what it reports instead of disabling the rule.

## Folder layout

```
app/                  routes — folders are URLs (page.tsx, layout.tsx, route.ts, ...)
app/actions/          Server Actions ("use server" files)
app/api/              Route Handlers
components/           shared React components
components/ui/        shadcn/ui components (generated by the shadcn CLI)
lib/                  server-side code and utilities
lib/db/               Drizzle: schema.ts, index.ts, queries/, seed.ts
lib/auth.ts           Better Auth server config; lib/auth-client.ts for the browser
proxy.ts              request proxy (NOT middleware.ts)
drizzle/              generated SQL migrations — never edit by hand
```

- File names are `kebab-case` (`event-card.tsx`); components are `PascalCase` (`EventCard`).
- Import through the `@/` alias (`@/components/header`), not long `../../` chains.

## Working with a student

- Make **small, focused changes**. Do not rewrite or reformat code you were not asked to touch.
- **Explain** what you changed and why — especially anything Next.js-specific (server vs client, caching, async APIs). The student must be able to explain every line they hand in.
- Do not jump ahead: don't add features, libraries or patterns the task didn't ask for.
- If a request conflicts with these rules, say so and suggest the correct approach instead of silently picking one.
- Never commit secrets. `.env*` files are git-ignored; only `.env.example` (with placeholder values) is committed.

# Next.js 16 — App Router rules

## Server and Client Components

- Every component is a **Server Component** unless the file starts with `"use client"`.
- Add `"use client"` only when a component needs state, effects, event handlers or browser APIs — and put it on the **smallest** component that needs it, not on a page or layout.
- Fetch data in Server Components with `await`. Do **not** fetch data in `useEffect`, and do not create an API route just so a page can call it.
- To put server-rendered content inside a Client Component, pass it as `children` (or another prop). A Client Component cannot import a Server Component.
- Props passed from a Server to a Client Component must be serializable: no functions (except Server Actions), no class instances.
- Modules that touch the database or secrets start with `import "server-only";`.
- Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` environment variables reach the browser. Everything else is server-only.

## Request APIs are async

`params`, `searchParams`, `cookies()`, `headers()` and `draftMode()` all return
**Promises**. Synchronous access was removed in Next 16.

```tsx
export default async function EventPage({ params }: PageProps<"/events/[slug]">) {
  const { slug } = await params;
  // ...
}
```

- Use the generated global helpers `PageProps<"/route">`, `LayoutProps<"/route">` and `RouteContext<"/route">` instead of hand-writing prop types. They are generated by `next dev`, `next build` and `next typegen`.
- `searchParams` values are `string | string[] | undefined` — handle all three.
- In a Client Component use `useParams()` / `useSearchParams()` from `next/navigation`, or React's `use()` on the promise.

## Routing and files

- Special files: `page.tsx`, `layout.tsx`, `loading.tsx`, `error.tsx` (must be `"use client"`), `not-found.tsx`, `global-error.tsx`, `route.ts`, and `default.tsx` in **every** parallel-route slot.
- `error.tsx` and `global-error.tsx` receive `{ error, retry }`. Call `retry()` to recover — it re-fetches and re-renders (stable since 16.3). `reset()` only re-renders; most tutorials still show it.
- `global-error.tsx` replaces the root layout: it renders its own `<html>` and `<body>` and imports `globals.css` itself.
- Only the root layout renders `<html>` and `<body>`.
- Route groups `(name)` organise files without changing the URL.
- Parallel routes: every `@slot` gets a `default.tsx` (the build fails without it once the layout has another route). A modal slot also gets `[...catchAll]/page.tsx` returning `null`, so navigating away from the open modal closes it. Scope slot layouts with a route group so they don't spill onto sibling routes.
- Intercepting routes count URL segments, not folders: route groups and `@slots` don't count. `(.)events` in `app/(marketing)/@modal/` intercepts `/events/…`.
- Metadata: pages set only their own `title` (the root layout's template adds the brand); `metadataBase` comes from `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` (`lib/site-url.ts`). `generateMetadata` uses the same loader as the page.
- `opengraph-image.tsx` / `ImageResponse`: flexbox and inline styles only, and any `<div>` with more than one child needs `display: flex` — `{a} · {b}` is three children; use one template string.
- Internal links use `<Link>` from `next/link`, never `<a href>`. Images use `next/image`; fonts use `next/font`.
- `next/image`: give `width` + `height`, or `fill` inside a positioned parent, plus `sizes`. Use `preload` for the main above-the-fold image — `priority` is deprecated in Next 16. Remote hosts must be listed in `images.remotePatterns`.
- Navigation hooks come from `next/navigation` — never `next/router`.
- Use `redirect()` and `notFound()` from `next/navigation` in server code.
- Request interception lives in **`proxy.ts`** with `export function proxy(request)`. `middleware.ts` is deprecated. The proxy runs on the Node runtime; do not set `runtime: "edge"`.
- Route Handlers: `export async function GET(request: Request, ctx: RouteContext<"/api/events/[slug]">)`, then `const { slug } = await ctx.params`.

## Caching (Next 16)

- Routes are **dynamic by default**. Caching is opt-in with the `"use cache"` directive.
- `cacheLife` and `cacheTag` are imported from `next/cache` — stable, **no `unstable_` prefix**.
- `revalidateTag(tag, "max")` — the second argument is **required**. The one-argument form is a type error.
- `updateTag(tag)` is for **Server Actions only** (the user sees their own write immediately). `refresh()` re-renders the current route.
- Once `cacheComponents: true` is set in `next.config.ts` (class 07), the segment exports `dynamic`, `revalidate`, `fetchCache` and `dynamicParams` are **not allowed**. Wrap request-dependent parts in `<Suspense>` instead.
- Do not use `experimental.ppr` — it became `cacheComponents`.
- With Cache Components on, every page keeps a static part and moves request-time reads (`searchParams`, `cookies()`/the session, uncached queries) into a child component behind `<Suspense>`. Awaiting them at the top of the page makes `next build` fail.
- `new Date()` / `Date.now()` in a Server Component is a prerender error: put it in a `"use cache"` function or read it after `await connection()` (from `next/server`).
- Keep cache tags in `lib/cache-tags.ts` and use them from there — never hand-type a tag string twice.
- A Server Action must expire a tag (`updateTag`) or call `refresh()`, or the page on screen won't update after it — not even an uncached page.
- Never cache per-user or per-request data ("tickets left", the session). Cache shared reads (`getEventBySlug`) with `cacheLife` and `cacheTag`.

## Removed or wrong — never generate

| Don't write                                                  | Write instead                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------- |
| `pages/`, `getServerSideProps`, `getStaticProps`, `_app.tsx` | App Router files in `app/`          |
| `middleware.ts`, `export function middleware`                | `proxy.ts`, `export function proxy` |
| `const { id } = params`                                      | `const { id } = await params`       |
| `import { useRouter } from "next/router"`                    | `next/navigation`                   |
| `next lint`                                                  | `eslint` (`npm run lint`)           |
| `serverRuntimeConfig`, `publicRuntimeConfig`                 | environment variables               |
| `images.domains`                                             | `images.remotePatterns`             |
| `unstable_cacheLife`, `unstable_cacheTag`                    | `cacheLife`, `cacheTag`             |

# TypeScript and tooling rules

## TypeScript

- `strict` is on, plus `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`: `array[0]` and `record[key]` are `T | undefined`. Handle the `undefined` case (early return, `notFound()`, a default) — do not silence it with `!`.
- Prefer `type` over `interface`, consistently.
- No `any`. Use `unknown` and narrow it, or the real type.
- Type-only imports use inline `type`: `import { type ReactNode } from "react"`.
- Once the database exists, **infer types from the Drizzle schema** (`typeof events.$inferSelect`) instead of hand-writing duplicate types.
- Do not add `baseUrl` to `tsconfig.json` — it is deprecated in TypeScript 6. `paths` works without it.
- `switch` statements need a `break` or `return` in every `case`.
- Match the real casing of file names in imports (`./event-card`, not `./Event-Card`). macOS forgives it; Linux deploys don't.

## ESLint (flat config in `eslint.config.mjs`)

The project enforces, and your code must satisfy:

- `@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports` — `import { type X }`
- `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` — unused variables are errors; prefix intentionally unused ones with `_` (`_prev`, `_request`)
- `eqeqeq` — always `===` / `!==`
- `no-console` — `console.log` is a warning; `console.warn` / `console.error` are allowed
- Next's `core-web-vitals` and `typescript` rule sets

Do not disable rules with `eslint-disable` comments to make an error go away — fix the cause. Never create `.eslintrc*` files; ESLint 9 uses flat config only.

## Tests (from class 10)

- `npm test` runs Vitest unit tests in `tests/unit/`; `PORT=… npm run test:e2e` runs Playwright against a production build (the port must match `BETTER_AUTH_URL`).
- Keep what you want to test importable: schemas live in `lib/validation/`, never only inside a `"use server"` file.
- Query by role and label (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`) — the same queries a screen reader makes. If a control can't be found that way, fix the markup, not the test.
- Never set `E2E=1` outside test runs: it exposes Next's testing API.

## Prettier

- Prettier owns formatting (with `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` sorting class names). Don't hand-format or argue with it; run `npm run format`.
- Do not add `eslint-plugin-prettier`. Prettier and ESLint run as separate tools.
- Don't change `.prettierrc.json`, `eslint.config.mjs` or `tsconfig.json` unless asked.
